system.name: ServerlessLLM
system.one_liner: a low-latency serverless inference system for large language models that optimizes checkpoint loading, live migration and scheduling

content.subject: how four scheduling policies trade off model-A and model-B latency when starting up B while A is still running

elements.name: Server 1 (S1)
elements.role: server whose GPU is initially idle while model A sits in DRAM and model B sits in SSD

elements.name: Server 2 (S2)
elements.role: server currently running inference of model A on GPU, with model B resident in DRAM

elements.name: Model A
elements.role: model A's weights, resident on S1's SSD or S2's DRAM/GPU depending on the policy step

elements.name: Model B
elements.role: model B's weights, the one being started up, initially only on S1's SSD

elements.name: GPU
elements.role: compute device that must hold a model's weights to run inference

elements.name: DRAM
elements.role: host memory tier, faster to load from than SSD but slower than GPU-resident

elements.name: SSD
elements.role: slowest storage tier holding a model not currently needed

elements.name: Load B
elements.role: time segment loading model B's weights into GPU memory

elements.name: Infer B
elements.role: time segment running model B's inference once loaded

elements.name: Infer A
elements.role: time segment continuing/resuming model A's inference

elements.name: Recompute A
elements.role: time segment re-computing model A's state after eviction, under the preemption-driven policy

elements.name: Live migration
elements.role: arrow marking model A's running state being migrated from S1 to S2 without a full reload

elements.name: A Latency
elements.role: verdict column reporting whether model A's inference latency stayed low (check) or was hurt (cross)

elements.name: B Latency
elements.role: verdict column reporting whether model B's startup latency stayed low (check) or was hurt (cross)

relations.what: S1 begins loading model B after the request arrives
once loaded, S1 runs inference on B
model A's evicted state must be recomputed after preemption
live migration moves model A's running inference state across servers instead of reloading
a model must move from slow SSD storage up to the GPU before it can serve inference

panels.label: (a) Availability-driven policy
panels.differs: S1 loads and infers B immediately while S2 keeps infering A uninterrupted

panels.label: (b) Locality-driven policy
panels.differs: S2 finishes infering A first, then loads and infers B itself since B's DRAM copy is local

panels.label: (c) Preemption-driven policy
panels.differs: S1 preempts to load A fresh and must Recompute A after a long interruption while also starting B

panels.label: (d) Live-migration-supported locality-driven policy
panels.differs: A's running state is live-migrated from S1 to S2 instead of reloaded

content.key_idea: Comparing four ways to start model B while A infers shows that only live-migrating A's state (not reloading it) avoids hurting either model's latency.
content.reading_order: top-left Setup boxes first, then down through the four lettered Timeline rows left-to-right, ending at each row's Performance verdict column

palette.used_for: white fill of the Load/Infer timeline segments and GPU/DRAM/SSD boxes
light gray fill of the Server 1/Server 2 outer setup boxes and alternating row backgrounds

style.arrows: mostly plain rectangular timeline segments; one curved arrow marks the live-migration hand-off in panel (d)

encoding.color_means: no colour coding is used; the figure is grayscale, relying on box labels, checkmarks and crosses instead of colour
encoding.line_style_means: solid black outlines box every segment; the one curved arrow in (d) marks the live-migration hand-off, distinct from ordinary segment borders

encoding.marker_means: check marks and cross marks in the Performance column report whether each policy keeps model A's and model B's latency good or bad

reusable_patterns: shared Setup diagram at top feeding four stacked identical Server1/Server2 Gantt-style timelines, each closed off by a checkmark/cross Performance column

sections: §5 Efficient Live Migration of LLM Inference (p.7)
evidence: Server 1 currently has Model A in DRAM and Model B in SSD and its GPU is idle
Server 2 currently has Model B in DRAM, and its GPU is running the inference of Model A
Our analysis is based on their impact on the latency performance of both Model A and B

summary: ServerlessLLM optimizes serverless LLM inference by speeding up checkpoint loading and adding live migration so GPUs are reused with minimal cold-start cost. This figure works through a two-server example: Server 1 (S1) is idle with model A in DRAM and model B on SSD, while Server 2 (S2) is busy running model A's inference with model B already in its DRAM. Four lettered, grayscale Gantt-style panels compare policies for starting model B: an availability-driven policy loads B on the idle S1 but pays a slow SSD load; a locality-driven policy waits for S2's local DRAM copy but delays behind A's inference; a preemption-driven policy interrupts A on S1, forcing a costly recompute; and the paper's live-migration-supported locality-driven policy instead migrates A's running state from S1 to S2 mid-flight, so both models keep good latency. Each panel closes with a Performance column marking A's and B's latency good or bad.
summary_zh: 该图用双服务器例子对比四种启动模型B的调度策略：可用性优先、局部性优先、抢占式和论文提出的支持热迁移的局部性策略，后者把A的运行状态从S1热迁移到S2，使A、B延迟都保持良好，其余策略均有一方延迟变差。
notes: verdict 'ours' on panel (d) inferred from it being the paper's live-migration contribution (section title), not stated verbatim as best in the excerpt.
